extracted.intended_audience: general readers, potential contributors, advertisers, press, and job applicants
extracted.subtask_description: The page describes The Onion's official policies and procedures for contacting the organization, submitting material (and its refusal to accept unsolicited submissions), advertising, licensing, archives, careers, feedback, and press/speaking requests. It is a publisher-level FAQ and policy summary for interacting with The Onion.

rubrics_metrics.name: No outside submissions accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: No, The Onion does not accept outside submissions of any kind. We will not respond to any unsolicited submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsolicited creative work, ideas, or manuscripts should not be sent; The Onion will not review or reply to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not send unsolicited résumés
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not send résumés unless specifically told to do so in a job listing. Any unsolicited résumés will be immediately discarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Onion Inc. posts openings on its Careers page; only apply/respond to positions explicitly listed there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising inquiry procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Please send all advertising inquiries to advertising@theonion.com. Please specify the business you would like to advertise, and the appropriate advertising sales representative will get back to you promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For more information regarding advertising opportunities, consult the Media Kit referenced on the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press and event/press inquiry procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Please send all inquiries from media organizations to press@theonion.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members of other media organizations should direct coverage inquiries to press@theonion.com; the same contact handles speaking-engagement requests for writers and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speaking-engagement requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The writers and editors ... are available for speaking engagements. Please send all inquiries to press@theonion.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagements include universities, conferences, meet-ups, and festivals; inquiries routed through press@ will be handled accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback submission and non-guarantee of response
rubrics_metrics.description: Please send all concerns to publicfeedback@theonion.com. The Onion cannot guarantee a response to any feedback to its content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers may submit feedback but should not expect a guaranteed reply; contact via the provided publicfeedback@ address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical website support procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: To report a technical issue with TheOnion.com, please submit a request through the Kinja support center with a summary of the issue and your browser information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide browser information and a summary when using Kinja support; this is the accepted channel for site technical problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: No unsolicited bulk email or attachments accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Please note that unsolicited bulk email, email attachments, and junk email of any kind are not accepted, and will be filtered and immediately discarded upon receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send mass emails, attachments, or unsolicited content via the provided contact addresses; such messages will not be processed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprinting and retransmission restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Onion may not be reprinted or retransmitted in whole or in part without the express written consent of the publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To license material, send a request to permissions@theonion.com; licensing requests are handled by that address and require written consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archive access and requests
rubrics_metrics.description: This website contains all of The Onion’s articles published from early 1996 through the present. For articles and graphics from past issues, including those published before 1996, send requests to archive@theonion.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can browse the archive by topic, tags, or search; the Onion will attempt to answer archive requests but cannot guarantee a response to all such requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy policy availability
rubrics_metrics.description: To read The Onion’s privacy policy, please click here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Privacy-related questions should be resolved by consulting the linked privacy policy page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of names in stories (fictionalization policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Onion uses invented names in all of its stories, except in cases where public figures are being satirized. Any other use of real names is accidental and coincidental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect characters and non-public-person names to be fabricated; real-name usage outside of public-figure satire is unintended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Onion is not intended for readers under 18 years of age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site signals an adult audience; under-18 readership is explicitly not the intended audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal/First Amendment stance on satire
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not do that. The First Amendment protects satire as a form of free speech and expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Onion invokes First Amendment protection as a defense to legal actions arising from its satirical content.
